newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's net international assets fall.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's net international assets fall.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said Wednesday its net international assets as of September 13, 1996, were $3.678 billion, compared with $3.851 billion on September 6.
The central bank said that its net international reserves as of September 13 were $15.426 billion, compared with $15.528 billion as of September 6.
It said the decrease of $173 million in net international assets in the week was due to:
- A net sale of currency to state oil firm Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) of $54 million, mainly to cover the firm's external debt payments
- A net sale of currency to the federal government of $68 million to cover external debt service.
- Other foreign exchange outgoings worth a net $51 million.

Banco de Mexico said the monetary base rose 3.085 billion pesos in the same period due to seasonal demand for notes and coins stemming from salary payments for the first two weeks of September, and the September 14-16 long weekend for Independence Day celebrations.

The balance of the federal government's account with the central bank fell by 6.800 billion pesos, mainly as a result of transfers of funds to state governments and the government's purchase of currency for external debt service.

Central bank credit to banks fell by 2.348 billion pesos to neutralise the effect of the federal government's withdrawal of funds from its account with the central bank, after taking account of the increase of the monetary base.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's assets and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six month duration from other central banks.
